newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon nationalist demands Syrian troop pullout.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon nationalist demands Syrian troop pullout.

text.p: A veteran Lebanese nationalist crossed swords on Tuesday with Syrian leaders, saying the continued presence of Syrian troops in Lebanon could lead to renewed sectarian strife.

Albert Moukheiber, 82, a fierce critic of the pro-Syrian Beirut government, contradicted a statement last week by Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam that those seeking the withdrawal of Syria's 35,000 troops were trying to shatter Lebanese unity and re-ignite civil strife.

Khaddam said it was up to the Lebanese state to request the withdrawal of the troops, who have been in the country since 1976 and have failed to pull back from Beirut in accordance with the 1989 Taif accord which ended the 1975-90 civil war.
"The continued presence of Syrian forces in Lebanon will blow up national unity and rekindle strife," Moukheiber retorted in a statement published in the conservative Beirut daily an-Nahar.
"We reject the Syrian vice-president's remarks and demand the withdrawal of Syrian forces," he said.
Many Christians demand the withdrawal of the Syrians, saying their presence is robbing Lebanon of its sovereignty and independence.
Moukheiber, a prominent Christian politician widely respected for his straight-talking nationalist views, heads an opposition Christian group called the Gathering for the Republic.

A former parliamentary deputy, he ran for parliament last year on a platform demanding the restoration of Lebanese sovereignty but was defeated by a pro-government candidate amid widespread allegations of electoral fraud.
Moukheiber said in his statement that Lebanon's civil war, which he called "the wars of others", was sparked by armed Palestinian attempts to share power in Lebanon.

"Today we say that Syrian sharing of Lebanese authority, in fact the total seizure of Lebanese authority, is the only factor that could blow up Lebanon's national unity and rekindle the strife," he added.
